Billa Radhakishan vs The State Of Telangana on 21 June, 2023
Hon'Ble Smt. Justice G. Anupama Chakravarthy

entities.text: Billa Radhakishan vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Criminal Petition No.7249 of 2022
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners/A-1 to A-8 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.1064 of 2022 on the file of Principal Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Gajwel, for the offences under Sections 498-A and 420 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,1961.

entities.text:
Principal Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Gajwel
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri T.Pradyumna Kumar Reddy, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the learned counsel for petitioners, Sri S.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 and Sri Gouraram Rajashekar Reddy, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
Perused the record.

3. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that bald allegations are made against petitioner Nos.2 to 8 in the case and even after span of 25 years, false case is foisted against the petitioners.
Therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

4. Further learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the incidents took place in the years 2002, 2003 and 2004 are mentioned in the case, which are at belated stage; that except the oral statement of the de facto complainant, no material is available on record to proceed with the case and that the allegations made in the complaint could not attract the offence under Section 420 of I.P.C.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that there are specific allegations against petitioner No.1 and therefore proceedings cannot be quashed against him.
He further submitted that general allegations are made against petitioner Nos.2 to 8 and therefore proceedings against them can be quashed.

6. Though learned counsel for the petitioners/A-1 to A-8 filed the petition for quashing the proceedings in the aforesaid Calendar Case, he restricts his prayer to the extent of dispensing with the appearance of the petitioners/A-1 to A-8 in the aforesaid Calendar Case before the Court below.
7. On a perusal of the charge sheet, this Court is of the view that truth or otherwise of the allegations made against the petitioners can be decided only after trial.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the proceedings against the petitioners.

8. In any event, considering the nature of allegations levelled against the petitioners /A-2 to A-8,
their presence before the trial Court is dispensed with, unless they are required by the trial Court for a specific purpose.
No such relief is given so far as petitioner No.1-A-1 is concerned.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.

It is needless to say that in the event of the petitioner filing an application seeking discharge, if the charges are not yet framed, the concerned Court shall dispose it of on merits within a period of four (04) weeks, from the date of filing after hearing arguments on both sides.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
